text: During peak harvest, several grain elevators go quiet. No pod crashes. No alert fires. The only thing that moves is one dashboard panel: pod count and cost climbing, while database load stays flat.
The HPA did its job -- fourteen pods, all running, zero restarts, correct labels. This isn't a crash, and it isn't the autoscaler. Something else is blocking these pods from reaching Azure SQL.

Pulling the Deployment and the NetworkPolicy side by side in kubectl finally shows it: the Deployment labels every pod app: grain-ingest. The NetworkPolicy, applied straight to the cluster weeks ago, selects app: ingest.
One word off. Kubernetes label matching is exact, not fuzzy -- zero pods have ever matched this policy. Every pod the autoscaler creates during harvest inherits a connection that silently times out.
The mechanism is proven. The fix -- and making sure this specific mistake can never ship again -- comes next.
